1Common Mistakes & Debugging Gotchas→2Symptom, cause and fix (quick diagnosis table)→3Further mistakes to avoid (not covered in th…
17.1Common Mistakes & Debugging Gotchas
Chapter overview

A consolidated list of real bugs found in this course's own example/template files — studying why each one is wrong is often more instructive than studying correct code.

# File The bug Why it matters
1 wk1ex3-student-template/index.html isNan(num2) instead of isNaN(num2) JavaScript is case-sensitive; isNan is undefined, so calling it throws a TypeError at runtime instead of doing the intended validation. Always check exact casing of built-in function names.
2 wk2resources/ex5.html <link rel="stylesheet" href="wk2ex5style.css" — missing closing > Browsers are very forgiving of malformed HTML and often "fix" this silently, but it's invalid and can break parsing tools, linters, or stricter renderers. Always close every tag.
3 wk2example7.html Duplicate style="..." attributes on one element, plus duplicate declarations inside one style string Demonstrates that "first duplicate HTML attribute wins" and "last duplicate CSS declaration wins" are two different rules — don't conflate them (see §5.4).
4 is216-wk4-student-template/Ex2.vue :width='wdith' — typo referencing an undefined variable Vue doesn't crash; the binding just silently fails. Always watch the browser console for Vue's "was accessed during render but is not defined" warnings.
5 Various .vue template exercises Using a hyphenated class name unquoted in a :class binding object, e.g. {-btn-primary: true} - is the subtraction operator in JavaScript — object/binding expressions with hyphenated keys must be quoted: {'btn-primary': true}.
6 Ex4.vue-style exercises referencing id2/similarly-named refs not declared in <script setup> Referencing a ref in the template that was never created Same class of bug as #4 — a silent no-op rather than a crash. Cross-check every template binding against your <script setup> declarations.
7 Conceptual (from Week 5 slides) Passing plain JS objects as an Axios/fetch request body without JSON.stringify (for raw fetch) or forgetting the Content-Type: application/json header The server won't parse the body correctly; req.body will be empty or malformed. Axios does this automatically for you — but raw fetch() (§3.4) does not.
8 Conceptual (§5.14) Assuming justify-content/align-items always mean "horizontal"/"vertical" Wrong once flex-direction: column is set — the axes swap. Always think in terms of main axis vs cross axis, not literal screen directions.
9 Conceptual (§5.15) Mixing fr units with % in the same grid-template-columns Percentages are computed against total container width, not remaining space — can cause the grid to overflow its container.
10 Conceptual (§10.2) Using PUT semantics (must supply every field) when you meant PATCH (partial update) A PUT request missing a field can unintentionally wipe that field to empty/null on the server if the backend implements true full-replace semantics — always check which one your API expects.
11 wk6resource/.../BlogPost.vue <img src="/src/assets/Angry.png"> referencing an asset file actually named angry.png (lowercase) Windows and macOS filesystems are case-insensitive by default, so this loads fine in local dev — then breaks silently (broken image, 404) the moment the project is built/deployed to a case-sensitive filesystem (most Linux servers). Always match asset filename casing exactly.

General debugging workflow (Chrome DevTools): 1. Console tab — check for red errors and yellow warnings (Vue's reactivity warnings show here, not as hard errors). 2. Network tab — for any Axios/fetch bug, check the actual request: was it sent to the right URL? Right method? Right body? What did the server actually respond with (status + body)? 3. Elements tab — inspect the live DOM to see what actually rendered, vs. what you expected your template/CSS to produce. 4. "View page source" vs "Inspect" — page source shows the original HTML sent by the server; Inspect shows the live, JS-modified DOM. For a Vue app these can look very different, since Vue builds most of the DOM at runtime.

17.2Symptom, cause and fix (quick diagnosis table)

Detailed explanations live in the sections referenced; this table is for fast diagnosis.

# Symptom Cause Fix See
1 CSS property ignored missing ;, typo in property/value (display: black), rgb(...,) check the DevTools Styles pane for a struck-through or warning line §5.2, §5.7
2 My rule "does not work" a more specific rule or a later equal rule wins raise specificity or reorder; check the Computed tab §5.4
3 top/left have no effect position is still static set relative/absolute/fixed/sticky §5.10
4 Absolute child lands in a corner of the page parent not positioned position: relative on the parent §5.10
5 width: 100% input overflows content-box adds padding and border box-sizing: border-box §5.5
6 Flex centring goes the wrong way axes swap with flex-direction: column justify-content = main, align-items = cross §5.14
7 Grid fr column overflows mixed fr with %, or content wider than 1fr use fr only, minmax(0, 1fr) §5.15
8 Bootstrap class does nothing Bootstrap 4 name (ml-3, data-toggle) use the v5 name §6.1
9 Grid columns do not line up columns outside .row, or no container container > row > col §6.2
10 Navbar always collapsed missing navbar-expand-{bp} add it §6.4
11 Dropdown/collapse/carousel dead JS bundle not loaded, or data-bs-* missing, or ids differ import the bundle; match data-bs-target="#id" §6.1, §6.4
12 Carousel shows nothing no slide has .active add it to exactly one §6.4
13 {{ x }} shows literally or errors not declared / not returned / typo declare in <script setup> §7.18
14 <img src="{{ url }}"> broken mustaches not allowed in attributes :src="url" §7.5, §7.8
15 Handler runs but screen same forgot .value count.value++ §7.4
16 Template shows [object Object] or RefImpl used .value in the template or forgot it in <script> script .value, template none §7.4
17 v-else ignored not directly after v-if keep adjacent §7.7
18 Console error with v-if + v-for v-if evaluated first wrap with <template v-for> §7.11
19 Class does not toggle hyphenated class not quoted 'text-danger': flag §7.8
20 Child does not show / "unknown element" component not imported, or lowercase tag <buttoncounter> PascalCase import and tag §7.14
21 Prop is undefined declared greetingMessage, passed greetingmessage pass as greeting-message §7.14
22 Parent is not told about a click child changed its own data emit an event; parent listens with @ §7.14
23 useRoute returns nothing not initialised: const route = useRoute() call once in setup §7.15
24 Axios table empty assigned the whole object instead of .courseInfo console.log(response.data) §8.5
25 "Failed to load" server not running, wrong port start the server; check API_URL §8.13, §13
26 Await error "only valid in async" function not async add async §8.2
27 Table not updated after POST/DELETE local array not changed push / filter / re-fetch §8.7, §8.9
28 POST returns 400 wrong or missing field names match server keys §8.7
29 CORS error in console server off or other origin check server and URL §8.11
30 Marks lost for v-html used where {{ }} is enough {{ }} §7.5
17.3Further mistakes to avoid (not covered in the tables above)

CSS

  • height: 100% when the parents have no height does nothing; use min-height: 100vh.
  • z-index without position (on elements that are not flex/grid items) has no effect.
  • Overusing !important and ID selectors leads to specificity wars; keep specificity low and flat.
  • A missing viewport meta tag makes mobile pages look zoomed out.

Bootstrap

  • Columns summing to more than 12 in a row wrap onto a new line (intended or not).
  • Mixing d-none with d-flex on the same element conflicts; use breakpoint pairs such as d-none d-md-flex.

Vue

  • Reading the DOM (window.innerWidth, element refs) outside onMounted.
  • Reassigning a ref variable instead of changing .value (count = ref(10) is an error for a const).
  • Storing response instead of response.data from Axios.
  • v-model on a text input without .number when you later compare numbers.
  • Missing .prevent on @submit, so the page reloads and state is lost.
  • Not clearing timers and listeners in onUnmounted (memory leaks).
  • Assigning to a computed (read-only by default).
  • Unscoped <style> leaking into other components.
  • Statements inside {{ }} (only a single expression is allowed).
  • v-html with user-supplied content (cross-site scripting).
  • Writing @click="fn()" when you meant @click="fn" (it runs with no event).

🗺️ In this chapter
1Tooling, Workflow and Exam Rules→2Running a lab-test project→3Lab-test rules extracted from the question s…→4Debugging toolbox
18.1Tooling, Workflow and Exam Rules
Chapter overview
Tool Role in this course
Google Chrome The primary execution/testing environment
Chrome DevTools "Inspect" for live DOM/CSS; "View page source" for raw HTML; Console + Network tabs for debugging
VS Code Recommended editor — enable auto-save (File > Auto Save)
npm / pnpm Package managers; this course's Vue projects consistently use pnpm (pnpm add axios, pnpm add bootstrap, pnpm install, pnpm dev)
Vite The build tool underlying every Vue project template here (vite.config.js, import.meta.env.BASE_URL) — provides the dev server and production bundling
nodemon Auto-restarts the Express server on file changes during development ("dev": "nodemon server.js" in package.json)
Postman GUI tool for manually sending HTTP requests (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) to test a REST API without building a UI first — inspect status code, response body, headers, and latency directly
MongoDB Atlas + Compass Cloud-hosted MongoDB cluster (Atlas) + a GUI client (Compass) for browsing/editing collections and bulk-importing JSON data
Git/GitHub Mentioned in the Week 1 syllabus for version control (not covered in depth in the files provided)

Common terminal commands used throughout Weeks 4–5:

bash
pnpm install # install all dependencies listed in package.json pnpm dev # start the Vite dev server (Vue) OR nodemon (Express, depending on the project) pnpm add axios # add a new dependency pnpm add bootstrap # ditto, for Bootstrap-in-Vue cd server/blog && pnpm install && pnpm dev # start the file-based blog backend
18.2Running a lab-test project
bash
cd client # (the question tells you the folder) pnpm install # once, downloads node_modules pnpm dev # start Vite; open the printed http://localhost:5173 link # in a second terminal for Q4: cd server pnpm install # or npm install node server.js # or pnpm start; check package.json "scripts" and the question script

[Wk4 slides "Quick Start"; LT26 Question Script]. Stop a server with Ctrl+C. The CourseInfo and bike servers listen on port 8000; Vite on 5173; the blog server also on 8000 (do not run two at once). Menu pages /q1 to /q4 are linked from menu.vue [LT26 menu.vue].

Diagram: the two processes in Q4 (inferred from the archive structure).

Browser: localhost:5173→Vite dev server: serves client/src/*.vue
Browser: localhost:5173axios calls →Node/Express: localhost:8000 /api→courses.json / bike_stations.json

Two terminals, two ports. If Q4 shows "Failed", check the second terminal first.

18.3Lab-test rules extracted from the question scripts
Rule Detail Source
Format 2 hours, open book, 4 questions in the order CSS, Bootstrap, Basic Vue, Vue + Axios [LT26/LT24 scripts]
Identity start every file you edit with a comment containing your name and email [LT26 Instructions]
No libraries beyond the given Axios and Bootstrap only [LT26 Q4]
v-html -1 mark per unnecessary use [LT26 Instructions]
Hard-coding do not hard-code data or messages the server provides [LT26 Q4]
Q1 vanilla CSS only; no Bootstrap; in 2024 no new selectors [LT24 Q1]
Q2 Bootstrap classes only; do not change IDs/text or add CSS [LT26 Q2]

19.1Selectors: what am I targeting?
Pick the selector by the situation
ScenarioSelector
every element of a typep {}

everything (reset)* { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; }
Specificity: inline > #id (1,0,0) > .class / [attr] / :pseudo (0,1,0) > element / ::pseudo (0,0,1). Tie → later rule wins. If your rule "does nothing", a class is beating your element selector. Avoid !important.
LVHA order for links: a:link, :visited, :hover, :active. Multiple classes: class="btn big" + .btn.big {} (no space) means both.

justify-content = MAIN axis, align-items = CROSS axis
ScenarioCode

navbar: logo left, links rightdisplay:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:center;

19.4Grid: rows AND columns
Use for page skeletons, galleries, calendars
ScenarioCode
3 equal columnsdisplay:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 12px;
fixed / fluid / fixedgrid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 200px;
1 : 3 ratiogrid-template-columns: 1fr 3fr;
responsive: as many ≥250px columns as fitgrid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr));
rows: header, body, footergrid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;
span full widthgrid-column: 1 / -1; /* or span 2 */
place by line numbers (end line exclusive)grid-column: 2 / 4; grid-row: 1 / 3;
named layoutgrid-template-areas: "h h" "s m" "f f"; header{grid-area:h} aside{grid-area:s}
centre content inside every cellplace-items: center;
7-col calendargrid-template-columns: repeat(7, 1fr);
implicit row heightgrid-auto-rows: 100px;
stop 1fr overflowing long contentminmax(0, 1fr)
fr = share of the remaining space. Never mix fr with % (overflows). N columns have N+1 lines; line -1 is the last. Flex vs Grid: content decides sizes → flex; layout decides sizes → grid. Grid for the page, flex inside the cells.
19.5Positioning & stacking
Offsets do nothing on position: static
ScenarioCode
nudge from its own placeposition: relative; left: 20px;
badge in a card corner.card { position: relative; } .badge { position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; }
centre an overlay exactlyposition:absolute; top:50%; left:50%; transform: translate(-50%,-50%);
full-cover overlayposition:absolute; inset:0; background:rgba(0,0,0,.5);
side menu that ignores scrollingnav { position: fixed; top:0; left:0; width:200px; } main { margin-left:200px; }
header sticks while scrollingheader { position: sticky; top: 0; }
toolbar pinned at bottomposition: fixed; bottom: 0; left: 0; right: 0;
image behind textimg { position:absolute; z-index:-1; }
bring to frontz-index: 10; /* needs a non-static position */
image beside textimg { float: left; margin-right: 12px; } .after { clear: both; }
fixed aspect ratio boxaspect-ratio: 16 / 9;
Absolute with no positioned parent anchors to the page. Absolute leaves the flow (neighbours collapse in), relative keeps its space. Sticky needs an offset like top:0.
19.6Tables, forms, links, lists, responsive
Typical component recipes
css
/* TABLE */ table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; } th, td { padding: 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #ccc; text-align: left; } th { background: #333; color: #fff; } tr:nth-child(even) { background: #f2f2f2; } tr:hover { background: #ddd; } table { table-layout: fixed; } td { white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; } /* FORM */ input[type=text], select, textarea { width:100%; padding:10px; border:2px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px; box-sizing:border-box; } input:focus { border-color:#58a6ff; outline:none; } button { padding:10px 20px; border:0; border-radius:4px; background:#2ea043; color:#fff; cursor:pointer; } button:hover { background:#238636; } button:disabled { opacity:.5; cursor:not-allowed; } input:checked { width:24px; height:24px; } /* LINKS + LISTS */ a { text-decoration:none; color:#58a6ff; } a:hover { text-decoration:underline; } ul { list-style:none; padding:0; } ol { list-style-type: upper-roman; } li { list-style-image: url(dot.png); } nav a { display:inline-block; padding:10px 16px; } /* padding works on inline-block */ /* RESPONSIVE (mobile-first) + dark mode */ @media (min-width: 768px) { .cols { display:flex; } } @media (max-width: 575px) { .hide-sm { display:none; } } @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { body { background:#111; color:#eee; } } /* ANIMATION */ @keyframes spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } } .loader { animation: spin 1s linear infinite; }
In Vue SFCs: <style scoped> = this component only; import './q1.css' in <script setup> for an external file. Scoped CSS does not reach child component internals.

21.1Template syntax & reactivity
What goes where in a .vue file
vue
<script setup> import { ref, reactive, computed, watch, onMounted } from 'vue' const n = ref(0) // JS: n.value Template: {{ n }} (auto-unwrapped) const user = reactive({ name: 'A' }) // objects: no .value, don't destructure/reassign const double = computed(() => n.value * 2) // derived, cached, read-only watch(n, (nv, ov) => { }) // side effect on change (ref itself, not .value) function inc() { n.value++ } onMounted(() => { }) // after first render </script> <template> exactly what the browser renders; Vue 3 allows several roots </template> <style scoped> this component only </style>
I want to…Template
show a value / expression{{ price * qty }} {{ ok ? 'Yes' : 'No' }} {{ name.toUpperCase() }} (expressions only, no if/var)
format money{{ price.toFixed(2) }} {{ price.toLocaleString('en-SG', { style: 'currency', currency: 'SGD' }) }}
bind any attribute<img :src="url" :alt="t" :width="w"> <a :href="`/p/${id}`"> v-bind="obj" (many at once)
boolean attribute<button :disabled="busy"> :checked :readonly :required
class: object / array / ternary<p :class="{ 'text-danger': err, active: on }"> :class="[a, b]" :class="x ? 'yes' : 'no'"
inline style<p :style="{ color: c, fontSize: s + 'px' }">
image from public/ or src/assets<img src="/assets/a.png"> or import pic from '../assets/a.png'; <img :src="pic">
unique id per item<div :id="`row-${i}`">
raw html (avoid: -1 mark, XSS)<p v-html="s">
comment out in template<!-- … -->
Plain const x = 5 is NOT reactive. Script needs .value, template does not. Quote hyphenated class keys. Never {{ }} inside an attribute.
21.2Directives by scenario
Pick the directive from what you need
ScenarioCode

loop with indexv-for="(item, i) in items" :key="item.id"
loop objectv-for="(val, key, i) in obj"
repeat N timesv-for="n in 5" (1…5)

typing / Enter / key@input="f" @keyup.enter="add" @keyup.esc @keydown.ctrl.s

hover@mouseover="on = true" @mouseout="on = false"
input ↔ variablev-model="x"

number / trim / on blurv-model.number v-model.trim v-model.lazy

21.3Exam patterns: ready-made logic
Copy, rename, done

// FILTER / SEARCH (computed keeps the template a plain v-for) const q = ref('') const shown = computed(() => items.value.filter(i => i.name.toLowerCase().includes(q.value.toLowerCase()))) // SORT without mutating const sorted = computed(() => [...items.value].sort((a, b) => a.price - b.price)) // text: a.name.localeCompare(b.name); desc: b - a // TOTAL / COUNT / AVERAGE / MAX const total = computed(() => cart.value.reduce((s, i) => s + i.price * i.qty, 0)) const doneCount = computed(() => todos.value.filter(t => t.done).length) const best = computed(() => Math.max(...items.value.map(i => i.score))) // ADD (clear form, trim, validate) function add() { if (!name.value.trim()) { error.value = 'Required'; return } items.value.push({ id: Date.now(), name: name.value.trim(), done: false }) name.value = ''; error.value = '' } // REMOVE / TOGGLE / EDIT const remove = id => { items.value = items.value.filter(i => i.id !== id) } // or items.value.splice(index, 1) const toggle = item => { item.done = !item.done } const start = item => { editing.value = { ...item } } // copy, then save back function save() { const i = items.value.findIndex(x => x.id === editing.value.id); items.value[i] = editing.value; editing.value = null } // DISABLED until valid / limit const canSubmit = computed(() => name.value.trim() !== '' && size.value !== '') // FIND / LOOKUP / CHECK items.value.find(i => i.id === id) items.value.some(i => i.done) items.value.every(i => i.done) list.includes(x) // GROUP COUNT items.value.reduce((m, i) => { m[i.type] = (m[i.type] || 0) + 1; return m }, {}) // DELAYED ACTION + CLEANUP const msg = ref(''); let t function flash() { msg.value = 'Saved!'; clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => (msg.value = ''), 2000) } let timer; onMounted(() => { timer = setInterval(() => sec.value++, 1000) }); onUnmounted(() => clearInterval(timer)) // TOGGLE / CYCLE / COUNTER LIMITS open.value = !open.value; idx.value = (idx.value + 1) % imgs.length; n.value = Math.min(10, n.value + 1) // FORMAT x.toFixed(2) Math.round(x) new Date().toLocaleDateString() str.slice(0, 50) + '…' `${a} ${b}` // STAR RATING '★'.repeat(r) + '☆'.repeat(5 - r)

22.1Axios: request cookbook
Every exam Q4 follows load → add → delete → display
javascript
import axios from 'axios' const API_URL = 'http://localhost:8000/api' const items = ref([]); const loading = ref(true); const error = ref('') async function loadData() { // GET: on mount, re-use to refresh try { const response = await axios.get(API_URL) // + { params: { q: 'x' } } -> ?q=x items.value = response.data // CHECK THE SHAPE: response.data.courseInfo ? } catch (e) { error.value = 'Failed to load' } finally { loading.value = false } } async function add() { // POST: body = 2nd argument try { const response = await axios.post(API_URL, { name: name.value, qty: Number(qty.value) }) items.value.push(response.data.item ?? response.data) // or await loadData() name.value = '' } catch (e) { error.value = e.response?.data?.error || e.message } } async function update(id) { await axios.put(`${API_URL}/${id}`, { name: name.value }); await loadData() } // PUT/PATCH: id in URL, body 2nd async function remove(id) { // DELETE: id in URL, no body (or { data: {...} } in config) try { await axios.delete(`${API_URL}/${id}`); items.value = items.value.filter(i => i.id !== id) } catch (e) { error.value = e.message } } onMounted(loadData) // several at once: await Promise.all(cities.value.map(c => fetchWeather(c))) // headers: axios.get(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } }) POST: (url, body, { headers }) // key in .env: VITE_KEY=abc -> import.meta.env.VITE_KEY (restart pnpm dev)
SituationCheck
where does the data goGET/DELETE: (url, config) POST/PUT/PATCH: (url, data, config)
responseresponse.data (payload) .status .headers
failure (non-2xx throws!)error.message error.response?.status (400, 404, 409) error.response?.data (server message) error.response undefined = server unreachable
"Failed to load" / CORS errorserver not running, wrong port/URL; look at DevTools Network
table emptywrong .data level; console.log(response.data) first
POST returns 400body keys don't match what the server expects
table not updated after writepush / filter / re-fetch the local array
show server message in UIalert(response.data.message) not a hardcoded string
StatusMeaning
200 OKGET / PUT / DELETE success
201 CreatedPOST success
400 Bad Requestmissing / invalid data
404 Not Foundid doesn't exist
409 Conflictduplicate / already taken
500 Server errorserver bug
Loading/error UI: <p v-if="loading">…</p> <p v-else-if="error">{{ error }}</p> <ul v-else>…. House style: named async function, try/catch, response/error, onMounted(loadData), no .then(). Use only Axios for HTTP.

* { box-sizing: border-box; } body { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; margin: 0; color: #1f2937; } /* =========================================================== PART 1 — GRID (2-column layout with sidebar) =========================================================== */ .page { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr; grid-template-rows: 80px 1fr; grid-template-areas: "nav nav" "side main"; min-height: 100vh; } nav { grid-area: nav; background: #18212f; } aside { grid-area: side; background: #f3f4f6; padding: 16px; } main { grid-area: main; padding: 16px; } /* =========================================================== PART 2 — FLEXBOX (nav bar) =========================================================== */ nav { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: 12px 20px; color: white; } nav .logo { font-weight: bold; } nav ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; gap: 16px; } nav a { color: white; text-decoration: none; } /* =========================================================== PART 3 — FLEXBOX (card row) =========================================================== */ .card-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-around; gap: 12px; margin-top: 16px; } .card { width: 300px; background: white; border: 1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; min-width: 140px; }

<script setup> // Import ref so values can reactively update the template when they change. import { ref } from 'vue' // Part 1: store the box ID and whether the box and button should use blue styling. const id = ref('demo') const blueBox = ref(true) const blueBtn = ref(true) // Part 2: store the text ID, its current color, and whether the danger button is shown. const id2 = ref('demo2') const activeColor = ref('red') const redBtn = ref(true) // Toggle the box between blue and red styling and toggle the matching button style. function changeColor() { // ref values are read and changed through their .value property in JavaScript. if (blueBox.value) { blueBox.value = false blueBtn.value = false } else { blueBox.value = true blueBtn.value = true } } // Toggle the text color between red and blue and update the button class accordingly. function changeTextColor() { // Check the current color before choosing the next color. if (activeColor.value == "blue") { activeColor.value = "red" redBtn.value = true } else { activeColor.value = "blue" redBtn.value = false } } </script> <template> <!-- Class names containing hyphens must be quoted because a hyphen is an operator in JavaScript. --> <div id="part1"> <!-- Bind the div ID and choose either blueBox or redBox based on blueBox's value. --> <div v-bind:id="id" class="m-2" v-bind:class="{'blueBox': blueBox, 'redBox': !blueBox}"> div ID : {{id}} </div> <!-- Always apply btn, then choose the button color from the blueBtn value. --> <!-- @click calls changeColor whenever the user clicks the button. --> <button type="button" v-bind:class="{'btn' : true, 'btn-primary': blueBtn, 'btn-danger': !blueBtn}" @click="changeColor">Change Color</button> </div> <div id="part2"> <!-- Bind the second div ID and set its text color from the activeColor value. --> <div v-bind:id="id2" class="m-2" v-bind:style="{'color':activeColor}"> div ID : {{id2}} </div> <!-- Always apply btn, then choose the button color from the redBtn value. --> <!-- @click calls changeTextColor so the text and button change together. --> <button type="button" v-bind:class="{'btn' : true, 'btn-primary': !redBtn, 'btn-danger': redBtn}" @click="changeTextColor">Change Text Color</button> </div> </template> <style scoped> /* Give the box a red background when the redBox class is active. */ .redBox { background-color: red; } /* Give the box a blue background when the blueBox class is active. */ .blueBox { background-color: blue; } /* Style a primary button with a blue background and white text. */ .btn-primary { background-color: blue; color: white; } /* Style a danger button with a red background and white text. */ .btn-danger { background-color: red; color: white; } /* Make the text inside the first demo white. */ #demo { color: white; } </style>

<script setup> import { ref, onMounted } from 'vue' import axios from 'axios' const API_URL = 'http://localhost:8000/posts' const posts = ref([]) // array of post objects const newEntry = ref('') // new entry to update the post const newMood = ref('') const toUpdate = ref(null) // the post object to update const status = ref('') onMounted(getPosts) async function getPosts() { try { const response = await axios.get(API_URL) // this gets the data, which is an array, and pass the data to Vue instance's posts property console.log(response.data) posts.value = response.data } catch (error) { posts.value = [{ entry: 'There was an error: ' + error.message }] } } async function updatePost(id, subject) { try { const url = `${API_URL}/${id}` const response = await axios.put(url, { subject: subject, entry: newEntry.value, mood: newMood.value }) status.value = 'Update Successful' console.log(response.data) toUpdate.value = null } catch (error) { status.value = 'There was an error: ' + error.message console.log('There was an error: ' + error.message) } await getPosts() // refresh the posts after update } </script> <template> <h2>Blog Posts</h2> <p v-if="status!=''">{{ status }}</p> <table class="table"> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Subject</th> <th>Entry</th> <th>Mood</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr v-for="post in posts"> <td>{{ post.id }}</td> <td>{{ post.subject }}</td> <td>{{ post.entry }}</td> <td>{{ post.mood}} </td> <td> <button class="btn btn-danger" v-on:click="toUpdate = post">Update</button> </td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <div v-if="toUpdate"> <h3>Update Post {{ Blog Posts · Axios DELETE — Example15wk5examples/Example15.vue

<script setup> import { ref, onMounted } from 'vue' import axios from 'axios' const API_URL = 'http://localhost:8000/posts' const posts = ref([]) // array of post objects async function loadData() { try { const response = await axios.get(API_URL) // this gets the data, which is an array, and pass the data to Vue instance's posts property console.log(response.data) posts.value = response.data } catch (error) { posts.value = [{ entry: 'There was an error: ' + error.message }] } } onMounted(loadData) async function deletePost(id, subject) { console.log('Subject to delete: ' + subject) let idx = 0 for (let post of posts.value) { if (post.subject == subject) { posts.value.splice(idx,1) // remove this element console.log(posts.value) break } idx++ } try { const url = `${API_URL}/${id}` // Payload must be inside the 'data' property const response = await axios.delete(url, { data: { subject: subject } }) console.log(response.data) } catch (error) { console.log('There was an error: ' + error.message) } } </script> <template> <h2>Blog Posts</h2> <table class="table"> <thead> <tr> <td>ID</td> <th>Subject</th> <th>Entry</th> <th>Mood</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr v-for="post in posts"> <td>{{ post.id }}</td> <td>{{ post.subject }}</td> <td>{{ post.entry }}</td> <td>{{ post.mood }}</td> <td> <button class="btn btn-danger" v-on:click="deletePost(post.id, post.subject)">Delete</button> </td> </tr> </tbody> </table> </template> <style scoped></style>

<script setup> import { ref } from 'vue' const teamA = ref("Falcons") const teamB = ref("Tigers") const scoreA = ref(0) const scoreB = ref(0) const step = ref(1) // points added per click const maxScore = ref(10) function addA() { scoreA.value = Math.min(maxScore.value, scoreA.value + step.value); } function addB() { scoreB.value = Math.min(maxScore.value, scoreB.value + step.value); } function reset() { scoreA.value = 0; scoreB.value = 0; } </script> <template> <div style="font-family: Arial; max-width: 520px; margin: 24px auto;"> <h2>Mini Scoreboard</h2> <p><strong>{{ teamA }}</strong> vs <strong>{{ teamB }}</strong></p> <p>Current: {{ scoreA }} - {{ scoreB }}</p> <!-- B. In-template expressions go here --> <p>Total points: {{ scoreA + scoreB }}</p> <p> Points left to win: {{ maxScore - (scoreA > scoreB ? scoreA : scoreB) }} </p> <!-- A. Event handlers go here --> <div style="display: flex; gap: 12px; margin: 12px 0;"> <button @click="addA">+ Team A</button> <button @click="addB">+ Team B</button> <button @click="reset">Reset</button> </div> <div style="margin-top: 14px;"> <!-- C. Display winner / status here --> <p v-if="scoreA === maxScore">Winner: {{ teamA.toUpperCase() }}</p> <p v-else-if="scoreB === maxScore">Winner: {{ teamB + '!' }}</p> <p v-else>No winner yet. <script setup> import { ref, computed } from 'vue' const x = ref(0) const y = ref(0) const lastResult = ref(0) const operators = ref(["+", "-", "*", "/", "%"]) const selectedOp = ref("+") const result = computed(() => { if (selectedOp.value == "+") lastResult.value = x.value + y.value; else if (selectedOp.value == "-") lastResult.value = x.value - y.value; else if (selectedOp.value == "*") lastResult.value = x.value * y.value; else if (selectedOp.value == "/") lastResult.value = x.value / y.value; else if (selectedOp.value == "%") lastResult.value = x.value % y.value; return lastResult.value; }) </script> <template> <p>x <input v-model.number="x"></p> <select v-model="selectedOp"> <option v-for="op in operators">{{ op }}</option> </select> <p>y <input v-model.number="y"></p> <p>---------------------</p> <p>= {{ result }}</p> </template> <style scoped> p, input { font-family: monospace; } p { white-space: pre; } </style>

32.1Appendix A: Pinia and Router Guards (Optional)
Chapter overview

Your Week 6 slides do not cover Pinia syntax. The only Pinia material in the archive is the Extra Exercises: Vue State Management PDF (task descriptions, tips such as localStorage + try/catch around JSON.parse) and the stores/ folder that create-vue generates. There is no solution file. The code below is (added context), standard Vue 3 usage, for recognition only.

javascript
// src/stores/counter.js (setup-store style) import { ref, computed } from 'vue' import { defineStore } from 'pinia' export const useCounterStore = defineStore('counter', () => { const count = ref(0) const doubled = computed(() => count.value * 2) function increment() { count.value++ } return { count, doubled, increment } // everything you want to expose })
vue
<script setup> import { useCounterStore } from '@/stores/counter' const store = useCounterStore() // same instance in every component </script> <template><button @click="store.increment()">{{ store.count }} / {{ store.doubled }}</button></template>

A router guard can redirect unauthenticated users to a login page:

javascript
router.beforeEach((to) => { const auth = useAuthStore() if (to.meta.requiresAuth && !auth.isLoggedIn) return { path: '/login', query: { redirect: to.fullPath } } })

When to use Pinia: when two unrelated components need the same data (a cart, a logged-in user); props/emits are for parent-child only. main.js already calls app.use(createPinia()) [wk5 example main.js].
